The University of Southern California (USC), founded in 1880, is a world\-class research university located in the heart of Los Angeles and the city’s largest private employer. As a USC employee, you will become part of the “Trojan Family”—the faculty, students, and staff who make the university an exceptional place to work.


USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences is committed to the creation, preservation, and communication of knowledge, a lifelong passion for learning, and the betterment of society. Realizing this mission requires a culture in which students, faculty, and staff can thrive—one grounded in respect, collaboration, opportunity, and a shared commitment to excellence.


The Director of Development will contribute to this mission by building meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, and friends and securing philanthropic support for the College’s highest priorities. In addition to strong fundraising expertise, the successful candidate will be a collaborative colleague who strengthens relationships, understands their impact on others, and contributes positively to the success of the advancement team and the broader Dornsife community.

**Job Summary**


USC Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences seeks an accomplished, entrepreneurial, and highly motivated **Director of Development** to manage and grow a portfolio of high\-capacity gift prospects and donors, with a primary focus on Hong Kong and a complementary portfolio in Southern California. This is a frontline fundraising role for a seasoned development professional who is energized by building relationships, identifying opportunity, and translating the intellectual and academic strengths of Dornsife into compelling philanthropic investments.


The Director of Development will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors capable of making **gifts of up to $5 million** and will be responsible for driving the full major\-gift cycle—from prospect identification and qualification through cultivation, solicitation, gift negotiation, and stewardship. The successful candidate will be an independent self\-starter who is comfortable creating a strategy where one does not yet exist, developing trusted relationships with individuals and families, and navigating complex philanthropic interests to connect donors with opportunities across Dornsife’s humanities, social sciences, and life and physical sciences.


Working closely with academic leaders, faculty, University Advancement colleagues, and other development partners, the Director will develop and execute individualized engagement strategies designed to deepen donor affinity, increase philanthropic investment, and secure support for Dornsife’s highest priorities. The role requires exceptional judgment, initiative, cultural fluency, discretion, and the ability to operate effectively across geographies, time zones, and levels of university leadership.


This is an opportunity for a proven major\-gift fundraiser to have meaningful ownership of a significant portfolio and to play a visible role in expanding Dornsife’s philanthropic reach internationally and in Southern California.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Build and manage a major\-gift portfolio.** Manage a portfolio of approximately 75 high\-potential prospects and donors, with a particular emphasis on individuals and families based in Hong Kong and Southern California. **Job Summary**

We have a unique part\-time opportunity to provide executive leadership for a California\-based client, a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting sustainable and reliable urban water supplies. This position is currently structured as part\-time; however, full\-time opportunities may be available based on the candidate's skills, experience and business needs.



In this role, the individual will serve as Executive Director, leading the client organization in achieving its mission to provide a unified voice for urban water solutions that support thriving communities and a healthy environment. Responsibilities include serving as a trusted partner and objective resource on California water issues, strengthening collaboration among member agencies, facilitating Board meetings, representing the organization at related stakeholder engagements, providing strategic counsel to support informed decision\-making, and managing/mentoring staff in the execution of the organization’s strategy.


**Job Description**



The Affiliate, Executive Director provides executive management services leveraging strong government/stakeholder relationships, excellent communication and facilitation skills, and a water policy background to implement the organization’s mission and strategy. This role collaborates with internal teams and external partners to contribute thought leadership on key issues. The Affiliate, Executive Director applies knowledge of California water issues, including existing and legislative and regulatory matters, and actively contributes to thought leadership within and on behalf of the organization. This role requires 8 – 12 hours per week.


**Responsibilities**


* Provide executive leadership and strategic direction to support the client organization's mission and long\-term objectives.
* Partner with the Board to develop, implement, and advance strategic priorities, goals, and organizational initiatives.
* Serve as a trusted advisor and objective resource on California water issues, emerging trends, and policy developments.
* Prepare and communicate issue briefs, strategic recommendations, policy principles, and other executive\-level materials to Board members and stakeholders.
* Represent the organization with member agencies, industry associations, regulatory agencies, research organizations, NGOs, and other key stakeholders.
* Facilitate collaboration and consensus\-building among diverse stakeholder groups to advance shared objectives.
* Lead Board and committee meetings, fostering engagement, productive discussion, and effective decision\-making.
* Support the financial and operational sustainability of the organization through sound stewardship of resources and the identification of potential partnership, sponsorship, or funding opportunities.
* Represent the client organization at Board meetings, hearings, conferences, and industry events throughout California.
* Manage and mentor a team, maintaining high\-quality standards, strong communication skills, and alignment with the organization’s mission, vision, values, and strategy.
* Flexibility to adapt and execute various additional assignments based on evolving needs.


**Skills and Competencies**


* Demonstrated executive leadership and strategic planning capabilities.
* Broad knowledge of California water resources, policy, and urban water management issues.
* Strong government/stakeholder relationships.
* Ability to influence, engage, and build consensus among executive leaders, boards, member agencies, and external stakeholders.
* Experience presenting to boards, councils, executive committees, and industry leadership groups.
* Strong facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to navigate complex and sometimes competing interests.
* Exceptional verbal, written, and executive communication skills, including preparation of strategic reports, issue briefs, and policy recommendations.
* Ability to synthesize complex technical, policy, and business information into clear recommendations and actionable insights.
* Strong understanding of organizational governance, strategic execution, and board relations.
* Financial acumen with experience supporting budgeting, resource planning, and organizational sustainability.
* Demonstrated ability to serve as an influential and credible representative of an organization with external stakeholders.
* Ability to work independently and adapt to changing organizational needs.
* Advanced communication skills with ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non\-technical audiences. \\
* Strong analytical, critical\-thinking, and problem\-solving capabilities.
* Sound professional judgment and discretion.

**Experience**


* Typically, a minimum of 15 years of professional experience in related role is required


**Preferred**


* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a technical, business, or relevant related field is preferred
* Water industry experience, executive leadership experience, and an established network within California water.
* Ability to attend Board and committee meetings and represent the client organization at meetings, hearings, and conferences held throughout the State.


**Salary Range:** The anticipated starting pay range for this position is based on the employee’s primary work location and may be more or less depending upon skills, experience, and education. These ranges may be modified in the future.


Hourly Rate: $100 \- $150



Benefits and Other Compensation: We provide a comprehensive benefits package that promotes employee health, performance, and success which includes medical, dental, vision, short and long\-term disability, life insurance, an employee assistance program, paid time off and parental leave, paid holidays, 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match, performance\-based bonus eligibility, employee referral bonuses, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance and long\-term care insurance. jobs.description:
**About VetPowered LLC**
========================


VetPowered was founded in 2009 to support Workshops for Warriors (wfw.org), an accredited 501(c)(3\) nonprofit school that trains, certifies, and places veterans and transitioning service members into dignified lifelong careers in advanced manufacturing to Rebuild America’s Manufacturing Force…One Veteran at a Time. Workshops for Warriors has trained and certified 1,776 veterans and transitioning service members, awarded nearly 23,000 industry credentials, and placed graduates at 522 companies across 49 states. The average starting wage for a WFW graduate is $63,500\.


Our goal is to train veterans for dignified lifelong careers and make America the world’s manufacturing superpower again.


That is the story almost nobody has heard. This role exists to change that, and to turn the telling of it into purchase orders, partnerships, and product revenue. This will allow us to create scholarships, provide housing, and build brighter futures for the men and women who honorably served our nation.

**Position Overview**
=====================


VetPowered, LLC is seeking a dynamic and highly organized candidate for the position of Personal Aide to the Chief Executive Officer. In this vital role, you will serve as primary support for a busy CEO, helping ensure smooth daily operations and efficient management of personal and administrative tasks.


The CEO has many time\-sensitive commitments, both professionally and personally, and is continually creating and pursuing growth opportunities for multi\-million\-dollar organizations. Your proactive approach, exceptional organizational skills, and attention to detail will help create an efficient and productive working environment.


Most importantly, this position requires patience, a pleasant demeanor, the ability to listen well, a sense of urgency, and the ability to follow directions. Reliability is a must.


This is a full personal and administrative support position and is not appropriate for candidates who wish to perform only in\-office administrative duties. Candidates with prior experience assisting very busy, Type A individuals are encouraged to apply. The information below is intended to provide transparent expectations for this key support role.

**Purpose of the Position**
===========================


At VetPowered, LLC, the Personal Aide exists so that the Chief Executive Officer can spend his time on the work that only he can do. The role removes recurring, time\-consuming, and personal tasks that would otherwise consume hours of every day or be improperly assigned to senior officers of the organization.


This position performs work that would not be asked of the Chief Operating Officer, Chief of Staff, or Executive Aide. That distinction defines the role.


The Personal Aide is accountable for the readiness and order of the Chief Executive Officer’s working environment, the continuity of his personal and household affairs, and the complete execution of any assigned task that is legal, ethical, safe, and consistent with the mission.


This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working behind the scenes to keep things organized. The ideal candidate will anticipate the CEO’s needs, maintain workspace readiness, and take pride in making his day easier. This hands\-on role requires discretion, flexibility, and the ability to thrive in a fast\-paced environment where no two days are the same.

**Duties, Responsibilities \& Expectations**
============================================

**Workspace Readiness**
-----------------------


The office of the Chief Executive Officer and all adjoining workspaces are the responsibility of this position.

* Ensure the office, desk, work surfaces, and adjoining workspaces are clean, cleared, vacuumed, and organized before the Chief Executive Officer arrives each morning.
* Maintain order in the space throughout the day and reset it at the close of business.
* No outside cleaning contractor, building custodial staff, or other personnel may clean or organize the personal space of the Chief Executive Officer. This work is performed by the Personal Aide.
* Maintain supplies, materials, and equipment so that nothing is missing when it is needed.

**Meal Service and Hospitality**
--------------------------------


Meals with senior staff and guests are a working instrument of leadership. This position ensures those meals happen properly without consuming the time of the Chief Executive Officer or other officers of the organization.

* Order, obtain, prepare, plate, and serve breakfast, lunch, dinner, refreshments, and snacks for the Chief Executive Officer and for guests or staff members he designates.
* Set the table and surrounding space in advance so that the Chief Executive Officer and his guests sit down to a complete and ready setting.
* Ensure meals are fresh, wholesome, and nutritious, while accounting for the dietary requirements of guests.
* Clear, clean, and reset the space at the conclusion of the meal without interrupting work in progress.
* Provide hospitality support for visitors, tours, and guests hosted by the Chief Executive Officer.

**Errands, Vehicles, and Personal Logistics**
---------------------------------------------

* Execute personal and business errands, including dry cleaning, laundry, shoe repair, shopping, purchasing, post office visits, pickups, deliveries, and returns.
* Provide basic dog care and complete other personal errands as directed.
* Travel to the residence and vehicles of the Chief Executive Officer to retrieve, deliver, or place items as directed.
* Manage personal vehicle administration, including registration, insurance documentation, service scheduling, and ensuring current documents are maintained in each vehicle.

**REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR \& EXECUTIVE SEARCH LEADERSHIP**



 Avenues for Youth is seeking a candidate for a contract position of Interim Executive Director. This is an opportunity to lead a growing youth\-centered organization partnering with young people experiencing homelessness and to facilitate an inclusive and values\-focused search for a new permanent Executive Director.


**ABOUT AVENUES FOR YOUTH**



For 30 years, Avenues has supported youth ages 16\-24 in Hennepin County. Whether a young person needs a place to stay for just one night, or a year and a half, Avenues partners with youth to find their path out of homelessness. We do that by providing a stable home, building trusting relationships, and supporting the youth’s education, career, health and wellness and housing goals. Avenues operates two shelter/transitional living programs for young people, one in North Minneapolis and one in Brooklyn Park, temporary supportive housing for young families, outreach and drop\-in services, and affordable housing for young people exiting homelessness. Avenues also operates two community\-based programs, our ConneQT Host Home Program and our scattered site, apartment\-based Avenues for Youth Families program. 2026 has been a year of significant growth for our organization – we closed on a capacity campaign, built a new building in North Minneapolis, and expanded programming.


**OUR MISSION**



Avenues partners with youth experiencing homelessness to achieve their dreams.



**OUR VISION**



A community where all youth flourish.


**OUR VALUES**



Avenues work is guided by the 9 Evidence\-based, Guiding Principles to Help Youth Overcome Homelessness and our core values: Equity, Community, Respect \+ Dignity, Trust, Liberation, and Anti\-oppression.



At Avenues, we believe:


* Homelessness does not define a person. It is just one part of a journey that we are here to help young people navigate.


* Nearly all youth experiencing homelessness have or are experiencing trauma. Therefore, mental health is at the center of all our work.


* There is no one reason why youth experience homelessness – it’s intersectional. Systems of oppression, racism and poverty are some of the root causes of homelessness. Without addressing these systems, homelessness will persist.


* Youth are resilient, inspiring, and the drivers of their own journey. With stability, trust and youth\-centered supports, their dreams can become reality.


**KEY ROLES**



With support from the Associate Executive Director, Director of Advancement, and the Director of Finance, the selected applicant will provide administrative, financial, personnel, and program management for the organization. They will oversee the day\-to\-day operations of the work, guide a diverse and talented staff, ensure the financial stability of the organization in a time of growth, and represent Avenues within the community and, to a more limited extent, with funders. They will also work with the Board of Directors to conduct a search for a permanent director. Avenues is a values\-guided organization – the 9 Guiding Principles and the 6 organizational values are key to who we are and how we do our work. It’s important that the contracted Interim Executive Director understand and live in those values as they provide leadership for the organization and the search for the next permanent Executive Director.


**LEADERSHIP \& MANAGEMENT**


* Work with program team to ensure excellent inclusive programming continues to support young people in finding and maintaining housing and exiting into safe and stable housing


* Work with the Director of Finance to maintain the fiscal health of the organization and plan resources according to programming and administrative needs


* Support the Director of Advancement in raising funds from government, foundation, and individual donors and communicating the work of Avenues in the community


* Partner with the Associate Executive Director in managing the human resources, operation, and infrastructure of the organization


* Ensure proper oversight of the organization by providing consistent support and updates to the Board of Directors, working in partnership with the Board Officers and Committee Chairs


* Ensure compliance with all federal and state laws and execute legal documents on behalf of the Board of Directors


* Serve as representative for the organization with funders, community members, government funders, and media (lobbying is not required of this role) EXECUTIVE SEARCH


* Conduct interviews and focus groups to identify the key competencies and skillsets needed for the next permanent Executive Director

* You enjoy mission\-driven work and feel aligned with our youth\- and justice\-centered values.



 • You have experience leading programs or organizations through times of transition. • You like to collaborate closely with a team and foster an environment of transparency and cooperation.


* You manage well in unpredictable circumstances and step up when help is needed.


* You can manage competing priorities and deal with multiple important factors simultaneously.


* You are ready to lead a group of engaged young people, staff, and board members in an executive search.


**TERM**



This is a temporary, contract role, with an estimated 25\-30 hours/week, not benefits eligible. **The Virgin Islands Museum of Art**

Operating as a kunsthalle with changing exhibitions, educational programs, public events, and community partnerships, the Museum will use art as a lens through which to explore the traditions, history, and cultural life of the Virgin Islands. 25 years in, Upwardly Global (UpGlo) has a proven program, a compelling case for support, and a major donor base that is far smaller than that case warrants. We are hiring a major gifts leader to change that, primarily by finding, qualifying, and closing donors who do not know us yet.


This is a build role, not a maintenance role. If your best work has been opening new relationships rather than inheriting mature ones, keep reading.

**Why This Role, Why Now**


Upwardly Global (UpGlo) is a national nonprofit that helps immigrants, refugees, and asylees rebuild their professional careers in the United States. We work at both the direct service and system\-change levels, building a more inclusive workforce and economy by ensuring everyone can fully use their skills and talents.

**Here is what that means for a fundraiser:**

* The case for support is concrete and measurable. We can show a donor the economic return on a placed professional, not just a sentiment. That is a rare advantage in a first major gift conversation.
* The prospect universe is genuinely underworked. Individual giving currently accounts for roughly $2M of our $14M in annual revenue. Our modeled major gift capacity is significantly larger, and whole segments of it (e.g., technology and finance executives, immigrant\-founder networks, family foundations, DAF\-advised households) have never been systematically cultivated at scale.
* You will not be prospecting alone. Our CEO, CRO, Board, and program leadership actively open doors, and we fund prospect research, wealth screening, and Salesforce so your hours go to donor conversations rather than data archaeology.
* The acquisition mandate is explicit. Bringing in new donors is the primary success measure for this role and is resourced and protected as such, not a stretch goal layered on top of a full stewardship load.

* Build a qualification plan for 40 new prospects and complete your first 20 discovery visits.
* Agree on a multi\-year individual giving growth plan with the Chief Revenue Officer and CEO.

**First 12 months**

* Personally close $2M from a portfolio of roughly 100–125 households, with at least 70% coming from donors new to UpGlo at the major gift level.
* Move 20 new prospects into active cultivation and secure 10 six\-figure commitments.

**By year three**

As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

**The Team**


Our Global Health (GH) division harnesses advances in science and technology to save lives in poor countries. We focus on the health problems that have a major impact in developing countries but get too little attention and funding. Where tools exist, we support sustainable ways to improve their delivery. Where they don’t, we invest in research and development of new interventions, such as vaccines, drugs, and diagnostics. Our work in infectious diseases focuses on strategies to fight and prevent HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, neglected tropical diseases, enteric and diarrheal diseases, pneumonia, and maternal, newborn and child health.
  

  

Our TB and HIV work is combined under a joint TB/HIV Program Strategy Team (PST), and focuses on research, development and delivery of new products and tools.  

  

The foundation’s Tuberculosis (TB) team aims to address key gaps along the TB care pathway through new approaches to protecting against infection, preventing progression from infection to disease, and improving diagnosis and treatment. Our efforts are diversified based on the understanding that vaccines, diagnostics, drugs, and improved care delivery are all essential to addressing the TB epidemic.
  

  

HIV remains a global epidemic that disproportionately impacts some of the most vulnerable populations. While ART scale\-up has led to decreased mortality and incidence, there remains a persistently high incidence. The HIV Program’s strategic vision is to accelerate the reduction in the incidence of HIV infection in high\-burden geographies and populations, and a main focus for the program is to develop new prevention interventions, including vaccines and biologics and enable their effective use as well as improving access and adherence to treatment.**Application Deadline: Saturday, September 19, 2026**

**Your Role**


This is a 9\-month interim role covering an exciting scope that balances program\-specific leadership, regional integration, and cross\-geography collaboration to maximize the Foundation’s impact on eradicating infectious diseases:

* **Program Strategy Team (PST):** The DDSPM will specifically focus on HIV and TB delivery within the PST, engaging closely with colleagues to ensure seamless integration of delivery and R\&D strategies. The role anchors the team’s planning, execution, and investment decisions, and supports delivery priorities with strong strategic and operational leadership. The DDSPM provides the link between the Delivery team’s technical expertise, strategy and business operations. Responsibilities include leading the strategic, financial, operational, and human resource aspects of the TB \& HIV Delivery team; providing senior business, investment, and management expertise to portfolio, domain, and investment\-level decision\-making; and overseeing annual strategy reviews, annual planning, reporting processes, and investment pipeline management. The DDSPM also leads a team of business and operations professionals.

Realizing this mission requires a culture in which students, faculty, and staff can thrive—one grounded in respect, collaboration, opportunity, and a shared commitment to excellence.


The Director of Development will contribute to this mission by building meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, and friends and securing philanthropic support for the College’s highest priorities. In addition to strong fundraising expertise, the successful candidate will be a collaborative colleague who strengthens relationships, understands their impact on others, and contributes positively to the success of the advancement team and the broader Dornsife community.

**Job Summary**


USC Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences seeks an accomplished, entrepreneurial, and highly motivated **Director of Development** to manage and grow a portfolio of high\-capacity gift prospects and donors, with a primary focus on Hong Kong and a complementary portfolio in Southern California. This is a frontline fundraising role for a seasoned development professional who is energized by building relationships, identifying opportunity, and translating the intellectual and academic strengths of Dornsife into compelling philanthropic investments.


The Director of Development will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors capable of making **gifts of up to $5 million** and will be responsible for driving the full major\-gift cycle—from prospect identification and qualification through cultivation, solicitation, gift negotiation, and stewardship. The successful candidate will be an independent self\-starter who is comfortable creating a strategy where one does not yet exist, developing trusted relationships with individuals and families, and navigating complex philanthropic interests to connect donors with opportunities across Dornsife’s humanities, social sciences, and life and physical sciences.


Working closely with academic leaders, faculty, University Advancement colleagues, and other development partners, the Director will develop and execute individualized engagement strategies designed to deepen donor affinity, increase philanthropic investment, and secure support for Dornsife’s highest priorities. The role requires exceptional judgment, initiative, cultural fluency, discretion, and the ability to operate effectively across geographies, time zones, and levels of university leadership.


This is an opportunity for a proven major\-gift fundraiser to have meaningful ownership of a significant portfolio and to play a visible role in expanding Dornsife’s philanthropic reach internationally and in Southern California.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Build and manage a major\-gift portfolio.** Manage a portfolio of approximately 75 high\-potential prospects and donors, with a particular emphasis on individuals and families based in Hong Kong and Southern California. Develop and continually refine sophisticated relationship strategies that reflect each donor’s interests, capacity, connections, and philanthropic objectives.

**Identify and qualify new prospects.** Identify, research, qualify, and engage prospective donors with the capacity and inclination to make significant investments in USC Dornsife. Develop networks and referral sources that expand the College’s pipeline, particularly within international markets. This work will be supported by research teams in University Advancement and Dornsife Advancement.

**Drive the complete major\-gift process.** Personally lead prospects through discovery, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, taking ownership of outcomes and maintaining momentum across a complex and often lengthy fundraising cycle.

**Structure Transformative gifts.** Partner with donors, their advisors, and university colleagues to structure significant and complex gifts that align donor intent with Dornsife priorities and university policies.

**Develop compelling philanthropic opportunities.** Work with academic and university leaders to translate Dornsife’s priorities into clear, persuasive, donor\-centered opportunities.  Avenues for Youth is seeking a candidate for a contract position of Interim Executive Director. This is an opportunity to lead a growing youth\-centered organization partnering with young people experiencing homelessness and to facilitate an inclusive and values\-focused search for a new permanent Executive Director.


**ABOUT AVENUES FOR YOUTH**



For 30 years, Avenues has supported youth ages 16\-24 in Hennepin County. Whether a young person needs a place to stay for just one night, or a year and a half, Avenues partners with youth to find their path out of homelessness. We do that by providing a stable home, building trusting relationships, and supporting the youth’s education, career, health and wellness and housing goals. Avenues operates two shelter/transitional living programs for young people, one in North Minneapolis and one in Brooklyn Park, temporary supportive housing for young families, outreach and drop\-in services, and affordable housing for young people exiting homelessness. Avenues also operates two community\-based programs, our ConneQT Host Home Program and our scattered site, apartment\-based Avenues for Youth Families program. 2026 has been a year of significant growth for our organization – we closed on a capacity campaign, built a new building in North Minneapolis, and expanded programming.


**OUR MISSION**



Avenues partners with youth experiencing homelessness to achieve their dreams.



**OUR VISION**



A community where all youth flourish.


**OUR VALUES**



Avenues work is guided by the 9 Evidence\-based, Guiding Principles to Help Youth Overcome Homelessness and our core values: Equity, Community, Respect \+ Dignity, Trust, Liberation, and Anti\-oppression.

* Homelessness does not define a person. It is just one part of a journey that we are here to help young people navigate.


* Nearly all youth experiencing homelessness have or are experiencing trauma. Therefore, mental health is at the center of all our work.


* There is no one reason why youth experience homelessness – it’s intersectional. Systems of oppression, racism and poverty are some of the root causes of homelessness. Without addressing these systems, homelessness will persist.


* Youth are resilient, inspiring, and the drivers of their own journey. With stability, trust and youth\-centered supports, their dreams can become reality.

Avenues is a values\-guided organization – the 9 Guiding Principles and the 6 organizational values are key to who we are and how we do our work. * You enjoy mission\-driven work and feel aligned with our youth\- and justice\-centered values.



 • You have experience leading programs or organizations through times of transition. • You like to collaborate closely with a team and foster an environment of transparency and cooperation.


* You manage well in unpredictable circumstances and step up when help is needed.


* You can manage competing priorities and deal with multiple important factors simultaneously.


* You are ready to lead a group of engaged young people, staff, and board members in an executive search.


**TERM**



This is a temporary, contract role, with an estimated 25\-30 hours/week, not benefits eligible.
